hook: Light reads out the electron spin of a palladium(I) complex and its phosphorus nuclei at room temperature.
summary: Circularly polarized pulses created electron spin coherence in Pd(I) complexes, and time-resolved Faraday rotation detected its coupling to nearby 31P nuclear spins in solution at ambient temperature. Results were checked against pulsed EPR and computation. This is a proof of principle on a model system, not yet sensing inside a working reaction.
title: Optical Access to a Molecular Nuclear-Spin Register in Catalytically Relevant Palladium(I) Complexes
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
